rationale: Agent cost grows faster than linearly because the whole history is resent each turn. A loop without a cap is a hard constraint violation, not a style preference. The session entry is a state machine rather than a loop, so its cap is on the whole run.

defaults.onBudgetExceeded: stop and escalate to a human with the partial result
defaults.onNoProgress: stop after two consecutive iterations with no measurable change

verify.stopCriterion: every applicable item in the governing checklist passes and the repository build, lint and tests pass once on the final tree
verify.escalateWhen: the same check fails twice in a row, or the suite is red for a reason outside the change
verify.iterationRequires: a new failure, an open finding or an unchecked risk; a check that passed is not re-run until the tree changes, and a file that was read is not re-read until it is edited

evaluate.stopCriterion: the evaluator score reaches the threshold declared at the start, or two consecutive iterations move it by less than one point
evaluate.escalateWhen: the score falls between iterations, which means the rubric or the task is wrong

session.stopCriterion: the review verdict is approve or approve-with-comments and the test stage reports a real pass; warn findings never hold a gate
session.escalateWhen: any phase returns blocked or escalated, the same phase returns blocked twice, or a finding is still open after the second review round
session.reviewRoundRationale: request-changes sends the blocker and major findings back to implement, then a re-review scoped to those findings and the delta. A finding still open after two rounds is upstream of the fix, not a reason for a third.
session.rationale: A track budget is the sum of the phase budgets it runs, so the cap and the phases agree. Implement is 60k because it works one task at a time; a task that needs more is two tasks.
